title: August and the Border
premise: Tamsin Quintana, a crash investigator whose family died in row twelve of Flight 4471, has spent twelve years in witness protection after testifying against the smuggling network that downed the plane. When a realtor's listing exposes their safe house — interior photos and all — Tamsin realizes the network never lost track of them; it has been selling them to buyers all along. With the help of Marisol, a border agent torn between duty and love, Tamsin must dismantle the training compound that created the network before the checkpoint shift change gives the hunters one last window. In the end, Tamsin trades anonymity for justice, burning the network's records at dawn while choosing to stay with Marisol rather than disappear again.
about_author: N. M. Villalobos is the pen name of a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade reconstructing accident timelines before turning to fiction. They write from a small town near the border, where the fog rolls in every August.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Twelve years after the crash, Tamsin works cold cases by day and memorizes escape routes by night, still counting rows on every plane manifest. A routine call about a listing for their safe house reveals interior photos taken days ago. The emotional beat: the illusion of safety shatters; grief resurfaces as fury.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Tamsin traces the realty agency to a shell company tied to the Vela network — the smugglers they testified against. Their handler, Okafor, insists it's a coincidence and orders them to relocate. Tamsin refuses, recognizing the photos were staged as a message: we see you. Emotional beat: defiance hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Nine
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. A border patrol agent who once processed Tamsin's paperwork, Marisol notices convoy patterns that don't match any official schedule. She flags them and is quietly reassigned. She reaches out to Tamsin through an old case number. Emotional beat: duty beginning to crack under the weight of what she's seen.

chapters.title: What the Training Built
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Marisol meet in a diner off the interstate and pool evidence: the network runs a training compound in the desert that manufactures operatives — and brokers 'disappeared' witnesses like Tamsin. The crash wasn't sabotage of a flight; it was a demonstration. Emotional beat: horror reframing twelve years of grief.

chapters.title: Okafor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Tamsin confronts Okafor, discovering he has been selling safe house locations to keep the program funded — Tamsin was inventory, not a guest. He offers a new identity in exchange for silence. Tamsin records the conversation instead. Emotional beat: betrayal transmuted into leverage.

chapters.title: The Shift Change
chapters.summary: Marisol learns the checkpoint rotates shifts in nine days, opening a window when the compound's supply convoys run unescorted. But her supervisor is on the network's payroll, and her inquiry triggers a flag on Tamsin's file. Emotional beat: love declared in operational terms — she chooses Tamsin over the badge.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The recording of Okafor goes nowhere — his superiors bury it within hours, proving how deep the rot runs. Hunters arrive at the safe house; Tamsin escapes through routes rehearsed for twelve years, finally understanding why the rules kept changing. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into clarity — no one is coming to save them.

chapters.title: The Compound
chapters.summary: Marisol and Tamsin infiltrate the desert compound during the shift-change window, guided by a defected trainee. They find the archive: flight manifests, bought judges, and the truth of row twelve. Alarms trip as Tamsin copies the drive. Emotional beat: standing inside the wound, refusing to look away.

chapters.title: August Fire
chapters.summary: Climax. Cornered at the checkpoint as the shift changes early, Tamsin broadcasts the archive to every newsroom and agency inbox before the network can wipe it, then torches the physical records. Okafor arrives to negotiate; Marisol arrests him on federal charges that finally stick. Emotional beat: justice seized outside the law, paid for in blood and smoke.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: Resolution. Months later, hearings unfold and Tamsin testifies under their own name for the first time since row twelve. Witness protection releases them from its rules. Tamsin and Marisol stand at the border at dusk, not crossing, just watching the light change. Emotional beat: belonging chosen freely — invisible no more.
